one_star_reviews.text:
Wouldn’t even rate one star!!

Found out I have gallstones after given birth, had several appointments with different doctors and not my own to discuss next steps, I was sent for a ultrasound to confirm it was gallstones nearly 2 months ago, I received a phone call from the trainie lady doctor who reassured me she was going to refer me to general surgery for removal of gallbladder. The trainie doctor wrongly referred me to a different department and has since left the surgery, so I have had to call the surgery to chase this to be told about the wrongly referral and that she was no longer there. An appointment was made for myself a week ago to see a different doctor in regards to me keep having gall bladder attacks, he promised he would send a referral a week ago which is still not been done. I called the surgery yesterday to be told to call back tomorrow as the DR missed parts off the referral form and he was going to complete this. I called back today to be told this was not the case and a referral has not been done, the lady advised me she was going to call the receptionist who was in yesterday as she was not in surgery today, so surely that means breaking patient confidentiality to be calling someone who is not in building to discuss about a patient. three hours went passed and still no call back so I called again and spoke to a different lady who advised she had red flagged this to the DR as urgent. fingers crossed this will be done. I think it’s disgusting patients trust DR with there health and get promised to be referred to find out nothing has been done at all.

This is not the first time we have had issues with this surgery.

one_star_reviews.text:
Sworders Auction House — an extremely disappointing experience

In my opinion, Sworders must rank among the most overrated auction houses in the country.

The first thing anyone considering using them should do is look at their published auction results. Compare the estimates they put on items with the actual hammer prices. The disparity can be astonishing. And before anyone trots out the usual excuse that “the estimate was deliberately kept low to encourage bidding”, let’s be honest: there is a very big difference between a deliberately conservative estimate and simply not knowing what an item is worth.

Calling every wildly inaccurate estimate a clever marketing strategy doesn’t make it one.

If you are consigning an important antique, artwork or collectible, you are entitled to expect considerably more than guesswork. You expect proper research, accurate attribution, meaningful provenance investigation, competent cataloguing, appropriate photography and, above all, an understanding of the market and the buyers who actually pay serious money for these things.

That is where I believe Sworders falls down badly.

Poor cataloguing doesn’t just make a catalogue look untidy. It can cost the consignor real money. If an item isn’t described correctly, isn’t attributed properly, doesn’t have its provenance properly established, or simply isn’t put in front of the right specialist buyers, then you are relying on luck. The right buyer might happen to see it — or they might not.

And that is the really frustrating part. An item could potentially have gone to a major London specialist auction house, been properly researched and catalogued, presented to the right market and achieved a substantially better result. Once you’ve sold it, that opportunity is gone forever.

For a consignor, “it sold” isn’t necessarily the measure of success. The question is whether it sold for what it was genuinely capable of achieving.

I also found the attitude of senior staff particularly disappointing. My dealings with Guy Schooling left me with an extremely poor impression. I found him arrogant, dismissive and lacking the level of professionalism I would expect from somebody dealing with valuable property entrusted to an auction house.

When you are potentially handing over antiques worth serious money, you need confidence that the people handling them know exactly what they’re doing and genuinely have your interests at heart. I certainly didn’t come away with that feeling.

My advice to anyone thinking of consigning something valuable to Sworders is simple:

Do your homework first. Get independent valuations. Speak to other auction houses, particularly specialist London houses. Compare their advice, estimates, cataloguing and proposed marketing strategy. And most importantly, look at actual auction results rather than simply believing the estimates printed in the catalogue.

The hammer price is the reality. The estimate is only an opinion.

And if the estimates are repeatedly nowhere near the reality, eventually you have to stop calling it bad luck.

At some point, you have to question the competence of the people making the estimates.

For me, Sworders would be very far down the list of auction houses I would trust with a genuinely valuable antique.

Buyer beware. And, perhaps even more importantly, consignor beware.

Have always wanted to try a nice meal here and took the opportunity to for my Nan’s birthday meal , menu looked good online and fairly priced and when we arrived we were shown to our table which was very sticky and in a dull area.

When it was time to order food we picked what we wanted on the app and every time we went to check out lots of items were out of stock E.G mixed grills , all steaks and fish and chips and when we questioned this at the bar is all steaks unavailable they said that the grill had blown , which wasn’t made aware to us on arrival when we were shown to our table ( which was pre booked ) and if that was brought to our attention we would of found somewhere else to go.

My wife wanted a cheese burger and there was no option to make it plain which just after we ordered the food and drinks I went out my way to ask for it to be plain ( no cheese , salad and sauce) which the woman said she will tell someone.

The wait for food was about 30-40 minutes and the drinks still weren’t delivered to the table at that time which again I had to go up and ask where are the drinks to which I got told that someone didn’t print a ticket which isn’t a good enough excuse.

The burgers didn’t taste amazing as they just tasted like frozen burgers you would get out the freezer section in Asda also my wife’s burger come with everything on it even though I made it very clear that I wanted the cheese burger plain which a new burger got made and that wasn’t hot at all with a slight pink in the middle , also the condiments were scattered all over the restaurant as there were no cutlery in the condiment station and no salt so we had to find it ourselves.

All round service just was rubbish and not one thought about customers by the staff from upon entering to leaving to which will be my first and last visit unfortunately.

one_star_reviews.text:
I drove into this establishment simply intending to fuel up, only to have a member of staff come charging outside towards me, waving his hands in the air as though I had done something seriously wrong.

There was no visible signage whatsoever indicating that the pumps were not self-service. Like most garages in the UK, I naturally assumed I was supposed to get out and fuel the vehicle myself. If this establishment operates differently, then put up a clear sign and politely explain it to customers. It really is that simple.

Instead, I was met with hostility, no manners, no basic courtesy and absolutely no attempt at customer service. The way this member of staff approached me was completely unnecessary and utterly unacceptable.

As a person of colour, I cannot help but question whether he would have come charging out, waving his arms and speaking to me in the same manner had I been a white customer. I cannot claim to know what was going through his mind, but I can say exactly how his behaviour made me feel: singled out, unwelcome and discriminated against.

And when I challenged him about his attitude, did I receive an apology or even a professional explanation?

No.

His response was simply: “Whatever, mate.”

Absolutely disgusting.

If customers are expected to somehow know that this garage isn’t self-service despite there being no sign telling them so, that is the establishment’s failure — not the customer’s. It certainly doesn’t give a member of staff the right to come charging towards someone and then treat them with contempt when they question his behaviour.

I came in to buy fuel. I left feeling humiliated, angry and wondering whether the colour of my skin played a part in how I was treated.

I will never use this establishment again. I would rather spend my money somewhere that understands basic manners, professionalism and, most importantly, that every customer deserves to be treated with the same dignity and respect.

I paid for a professional brow wax and tint and would expect a much higher standard. I have contacted BROWS directly to make a formal complaint and am requesting a refund.

I would not recommend based on my experience today.

one_star_reviews.text:
In November 2022 I paid Howdens just over £3000 for a quantity of solid prefinished block square edged worktop in grey oak.
In June of this year a 2 feet hairline crack appeared on the breakfast bar. I was told by my carpenter who installed the work tops that this should never have happened in good and authentic hard wood. When we made a complaint to Howdens they denied any culpability and outrageously accused me of dropping something heavy on it . Just think how ridiculous that sounds. However they informed me that they had withdrawn this particular product from sale. No explanation was given . So this leads me to believe that they discovered that the product was inherently faulty. Why else would they withdraw it?
We also found that despite our best efforts to keep the worktops mark free, it very easily and permanently stained .This meant that we had to regularly sand it and re-stain it with Howdens own staining product. Was this another reason why it was withdrawn? Howdens then told us that they no longer stock the stain and they refused to sell us the 3 tins they had left across the country on the basis they were ‘out of date’ would you believe? So that has left us high and dry
I cannot believe that a company such has Howdens has acted so inappropriately and probably dishonestly and denying any liability and compensation. Shame on you.Potential customers beware

The Imam's khutbahs are, in my experience, often divisive, with negative comments about other faiths and cultures. I believe our sermons should encourage respect, understanding, and unity within our diverse community.

This was particularly disappointing during the Eid khutbah, which was broadcast over loudspeakers and could be heard by many surrounding homes. As Muslims living alongside people of different faiths, I think we should consider how our neighbours feel when they hear comments that could be perceived as critical of Christians or dismissive of science. I worry that this risks damaging community relations rather than strengthening them. We then sit here and complain as to why the community are against Muslims when we show such division ourselves.

On a positive note, the parking attendants were excellent and worked extremely hard to manage the traffic. The Eid in the Park event itself was very well organised, with great food stalls and plenty of activities for children. Credit should go to everyone involved in making the event enjoyable for families.

one_star_reviews.text:
I have genuinely never had such a poor experience at a gym.
I signed up for the 7-day trial at Strong Girl Collective specifically because they offer baby-friendly hours. I followed all of the instructions I received by email to activate my membership, and nowhere in the sign-up process or the emails I received was I told that I needed to provide a medical report before attending.
When I arrived with my baby during the advertised baby-friendly hours, the receptionist stopped me at the door and refused to let me in because of this supposedly required medical report. I showed her the emails I had received, which clearly did not mention this requirement, but rather than trying to resolve the issue or contact someone on their side, I was simply advised to call the person in charge myself.
By this point my baby was becoming increasingly fussy, and after being made to stand outside trying to sort out an issue that should never have happened in the first place, I decided to leave.
The most upsetting part was that I ended up nursing my baby in a parking lot, after I planned whole feeding schedule around attending gym today , and despite having a full 7-day membership and being literally a few metres away from a gym that advertises itself as welcoming to mothers and babies
I completely understand that gyms can have policies and that certain documentation may sometimes be required. What I don’t understand is why this wasn’t communicated before I signed up or arrived, and why there was absolutely no attempt to help resolve the situation when I was standing at the door with a hungry, increasingly upset baby.
The whole experience was embarrassing, upsetting and completely unnecessary. I have never felt so unwelcome in a gym, and unfortunately this was enough to make me certain I won’t be returning .

My biggest regret was bringing these shoes here in the first place. Please believe the negative reviews — I wish I had!

one_star_reviews.text:
Avoid this branch at all costs. The word scam appears frequently in their reviews and my recent experience makes it very easy to see why. I was unexpectedly hit with a £110 bill after returning my car, consisting of £75 for a microscopic surface speck on the windscreen and a £35 admin fee.

When I picked up the car, the finishing touches were completely missed. The exterior had dried water marks from improper drying, the interior was covered in smears, and the windscreen still had flecks of dust and dirt scattered across it. Crucially, I was never provided with their vehicle condition inspection guide highlighting damage hotspots prior to my rental. They only decided to show me this guide after they had already charged me. Because the glass was dirty at handover, it was impossible to spot a tiny sub-1mm dot before driving off.

It is clearly pre-existing wear from a previous driver. The branch seems to take advantage of people who do not know about BVRLA industry guidelines, which classify sub-1mm surface pits as standard fair wear and tear. Instead, they classify it as chargeable damage to take your money.

The checkout was handled by Ahmed S. When I challenged the charge and asked for a second opinion, he brought out Mahfuj Bakth C. Mahfuj simply told me I had to email the branch with pictures to try and claim it back. It is incredibly unfair that disputes are handled internally by the exact same branch management that profits from the charges, rather than an independent customer service department. They act as their own judge and jury with no proper escalation process in place.

On top of the questionable damage charges, you have to be very careful with their add-ons. The advertised base cost is misleading because they lock you into a strict limit of 100 miles a day. If you go over that, you are penalized with a 30p per mile charge, or forced to pay an extra £20 or £32 for unlimited mileage upfront.

I have rented over 40 cars in the last 8 years from almost every major company including Alamo, Enterprise, and Sixt, and I have never been charged for damage once. If you absolutely must use this branch, make sure you factor the cost of their most expensive excess insurance option into your daily rate. Otherwise, they will definitely find a way to take a chunk out of your £150 security deposit.

one_star_reviews.text: I have limited company. Before contract I asked if AMB are able to pay my invoices through my limited company and I was told this was not a problem. Started contract. Ended up being forced sneakily on to umbrella company and was expecting me to pay £20 per invoice. Which is operating outside of the law. I refused and notified them if they wanted to bankroll their company using an umbrella company then the charges are to be covered by them. An invoice from a limited company is an itemised bill. It must be paid in full. Less CIS if required. This is different if you are PAYE or sole trader. But not for limited company. Didn't pay me. Had to seek legal action before they paid me. Still chasing up unpaid invoices now with the DASA umbrella company. Getting very close to me starting CCJ process against them. There is no need to do this. Not happy at all. I am a professional contractor and professional engineer. And things like do not help anyone. Just be aware. Get your contract in writing and payment route in writing from AMB so you have some comeback before you start contract. Otherwise you are going to get hit with large umbrella fees that they omit to tell you about. Seek some legal advice and/or use your own umbrella company. Apart from payment, or lack of it. AMB seemed a good company and the people seemed pleasant and nice to work for. Lots of feedback regarding job. But then again, they would and that is in their interest and it is exactly what I would do. So not unexpected really. Just the pay side of things that really annoyed me. I can work around pay problems and support a company as long as I am told the truth. But they don't tell the truth when it comes to pay. And things like that just make things worse. one_star_reviews.text: I’ve been left very confused and extremely upset by my experience. I enquired last week and visited Jonah on Wednesday, the volunteers are amazing and lovely. Lisa, Lisa’s son and Hilary all visited my home yesterday and met my beautiful 10 month old kitten who I’ve had from 5 weeks old and can clearly be seen to be loved, healthy and safe, this was even commented on by Hilary. We were at the point of signing the adoption paperwork when Lisa advised that she had been given the wrong paperwork by Hillary and had one for a dog not a cat. Lisa expressed her dissatisfaction towards her mother that this had happened and became quite snappy and stressed. Hilary seemed quite happy to list the rules to me and Lisa’s son even suggested sending them digitally but Lisa wasn’t having any of it. Lisa then advised they would need to think about how to get it sorted. I offered to pay the fee and also messaged later to say I would drive to Lisa to get the paperwork signed so that she wasn’t inconvenienced. I woke up this morning to a message saying we’ve decided to fail your home check and not proceed. No explanation given. I have been a cat mum for 20 yrs, my home is safe and not on a main road, my boys are 20 & 14 so not young children and no concerns were raised during the visit apart from that my living room is too big for a kitten, I agreed to start Jonah off in a smaller room. I feel so sad for poor Jonah who is currently living in a cat house in the garden of a home that is empty when he could’ve had a loving home in a safe environment with our family. There are so many kittens out there that need homes and yet this charity is turning down genuine decent people. I hope you find your forever home Jonah

Rating: ★☆☆☆☆ (1/5)

​As a parent whose son has now completed the two-year program at Shrewsbury Town Football Club College, I cannot in good conscience recommend this course. My overall impression is that it is extremely poor, lacks value, and fails to set students up for a successful future.

​Lack of Coaching and Development:
If you are expecting structured football training and athletic development, look elsewhere. At almost every opportunity, players were simply left to play unstructured games. There was virtually no genuine feedback, zero encouragement, and no actual training or instruction delivered by the staff.

​Unchallenged Bullying and Poor Staff
Oversight:
Bullying—both on and off the pitch—was ignored and left completely unchallenged by college staff. As a parent, I was forced to intervene directly and push the administration to take any action whatsoever regarding student welfare.

​Unprofessional Behavior:
While the college advertises football trips abroad as a key benefit, our experience was alarming. My son withdrew at the last minute from a trip I had already paid for, which turned out to be a massive relief given what transpired. The trip involved excessive alcohol consumption, which alarmingly included the staff members present.

​Verdict:
This program falls far short of providing a supportive, professional, or educational environment for young athletes. I strongly encourage any parent or prospective student to look for alternative options.

one_star_reviews.text:
Many issues. Firstly I'll give positive points: Staff were friendly. Burgers were tasty. We had a few allergen orders at our table, staff did very well taking the orders and appeared to understand the potential hazards, and were reassuring enough that we had faith enough to order.

Unfortunately this brings me to the negatives:
One of the coeliac folk in our party found batter in their chips. They began reacting while on the premises, but concerns were brushed off when raised. The other coeliac found more than half of the whitebait to be flaccid and gave up eating them. They stopped eating their salad when they found mushy leaves and grit. Again this concern was brushed off. They have also returned to their holiday base with the beginnings of a reaction.

The non allergen person in our party was disappointed with the onion rings, they apparently tasted of nothing but oil. These were removed from the bill but nothing else was.

When we'd been asked by staff who checked early on whether everything was ok, at that point it had been ok. Nobody had encountered anything untoward by then.

In all, to be charged this much money for 4 people to not complete their meals; two of whom will now be ill for days thanks to reactions, I would urge anyone with coeliac disease or even gluten intolerance to avoid the place.
Group size
10-30 min
Recommendation for vegetarians
Vegetarian offerings
Clearly labeled vegetarian dishes
Dietary restrictions
The menu is good, explains well what's gluten free and they understood other allergies and autoimmune conditions; however both coeliac folk in our party are reacting so probably not great.
Parking space
Plenty of parking
Parking options
Free parking lot
Wheelchair accessibility
Disabled loo is accessed through two doors, one normal disabled loo door and one heavy half glass door. In all honesty if I was in my chair, (ambulatory user) I still would have needed assistance. Dining room is quite packed down that end too, leaving no space for manoeuvre. After the heavy outer door, there is a 90° turn down a narrow corridor. Disabled loo was serviceable but could do with a spruce.

one_star_reviews.text:
We would’ve been happy with a simple extension to make our terrace home simply function as a 2 bedroom house.

However, the path we were forced down was that of a much larger extension more detrimental to our neighbours.

I hate leaving such a review, but Richard Biddle’s involvement was… beyond belief.

All this happened, as our neighbours enlisted Richard Biddle to help oppose our planning application, and the result was catastrophic for all.

Rather than simply talk to us, a war was unleashed.

Despite simple facts which were clear to all professionals involved, Richard Biddle failed to realise our neighbours had built significantly larger extensions than what we had planned - making the onslaught of planning objections little more than a barrage of entitlement.

NIMBYism in it’s purest form - “we built a large extension first, which gives us the right to say you can’t”

Ironically only one objection mattered - one which our neighbours neither cared about nor understood. Yet it meant our existing 90s extension would need to be demolished, forcing our second planning application to be a full rebuild, far more detrimental to our neighbours (Richard Biddle’s clients).

The objection was the use of zinc as a “shiny material”.

We required zinc in the construction to extend 2m on top of an existing extension with a concrete roof. Brick wasn’t an option without a rebuild.

Being forced to rebuild meant we would need to use the full width of the land to make the cost viable, and that meant an 8m long wall alongside their glass lean-to (built without compliance on top of the shared boundary wall).

For this planning application, even the credibility of our architect and the professionalism of the planning officer featured in Richard Biddle’s objections - and what professional uses that tact on record?

We would’ve been more than happy with a small 2m upstairs extension to give us a usable 2nd bedroom, and we would’ve been happy with a simple glass conservatory at the back.

Some simple consideration rather than the ridiculous circus unleashed with Richard Biddle’s involvement - and a simple knock on our door and a rational grown up conversation, would have been unbelievably more constructive.

I hope Richard Biddle was not paid for his involvement.

Unfortunately, I had a very disappointing experience with Low Cost Car Rental.

I reserved the vehicle a few months in advance and even called a few days before collection to make sure everything was ready. I was told that everything was good to go. However, when I arrived to collect the vehicle, I was given an over 20-year-old minivan with no cruise control and, most importantly, no air conditioning.

This was during the summer when temperatures were over 90°F, so having no air conditioning made driving the van extremely uncomfortable. What frustrated me most was that nobody told me in advance that the vehicle had no working air conditioning. They also did not have another vehicle available to swap it with.

If I had been told a week or more beforehand, I could have cancelled and rented from another company instead. Instead, I was left having to use an extremely hot van for my entire trip.

I was also disappointed that no discount or compensation was offered despite such an important feature being unavailable.

Overall, it was a miserable experience driving the vehicle in that heat. Better communication beforehand would have made a huge difference. I would not rent from Low Cost Car Rental again based on this experience.

Very Disappointing Service – Incorrect Wheel Alignment

I visited this garage to have my car’s wheel alignment checked and adjusted. I was told that, because my car is a Mercedes, the rear alignment could not be adjusted and that this was apparently the case with Mercedes and BMW vehicles.

I accepted what I was told and paid for the service. However, I was very disappointed to discover later that this information was incorrect. I went to another garage to have the alignment checked, and they were able to properly adjust the alignment on both the front and rear wheels.

This makes me question what service I actually paid for in the first place. In my opinion, if the rear alignment was not going to be properly checked or adjusted, I should have been informed clearly before paying for the service.

I contacted the garage by email on 5 August and requested a refund, as I did not feel that I had received the service I had paid for. Unfortunately, as of 24 August, I have still received no response whatsoever.

I am extremely disappointed, not only with the service itself, but also with the complete lack of communication afterwards. A simple response to my email would have been appreciated.

Based on my experience, I cannot recommend this garage. I strongly suggest getting a second opinion before paying for a wheel alignment here, especially if you are told that the rear alignment cannot be adjusted on a Mercedes or BMW.

one_star_reviews.text:
I purchased a 2018 Volvo V90 for £22,900 from Volvo Cars Chester through the Volvo Selekt Approved Used scheme in August 2025.

Within six months the vehicle developed a serious water ingress issue which resulted in electrical faults and over £1,000 of water-related repair costs. The issue was diagnosed by a Volvo main dealer as a failed sunroof seal.

Although the vehicle was still covered by the Volvo Selekt warranty supplied with the car, I was advised the water ingress issue was not covered and ultimately paid over £1,000 towards repairs.

Despite multiple repair attempts and repeated assurances that the vehicle had been repaired, water continues to be found beneath the carpets following rainfall and the vehicle remains subject to further investigation.

What has disappointed me most has been Volvo Cars Chester's handling of the situation.

The dealership was made aware of the issue within six months of purchase, yet communication has been extremely poor. On more than one occasion I was advised the matter was being referred internally to management, only to then hear nothing further for extended periods.

After contacting Chester again in May 2026, Paul Oddy replied:

"Apologies I will resend to Adam Cartwright to see if he can assist."

This was the second time I had been advised the matter was being escalated internally.

Despite being the supplying dealer, Volvo Cars Chester declined to make any contribution towards the repair costs and I have ultimately had to involve Volvo UK, who have now raised a formal complaint.

As things stand, I am still waiting to hear directly from Volvo Cars Chester management.

I note that many responses to negative reviews encourage customers to contact the Aftersales Manager directly. In my experience, doing so did not lead to any meaningful progress and I ultimately had to involve Volvo UK to obtain further engagement.

Before this vehicle I owned both a Volvo V70 and XC70 and they were excellent cars. They were a large part of the reason I remained loyal to the Volvo brand.

I appreciate that faults can occur on any vehicle. What matters is how those faults are dealt with. Based on my experience, I would encourage anyone considering a Volvo Selekt Approved Used vehicle from Volvo Cars Chester to think carefully about how any issues may be handled after the sale.

Unfortunately, this experience has left me with very little confidence in Volvo Cars Chester's communication, customer care and willingness to engage when serious problems arise after a sale.

Update 16/6/26. Chester are much faster at responding to a Google review than a formal complaint.

Update 16/8/26. Chester's response refers to a warranty decision made by “another company”. That company was Volvo Cars Shrewsbury, another authorised Volvo main dealer, who ultimately carried out extensive repairs.

Volvo UK has since confirmed in writing that responsibility for the sale, aftersales support and handling of my retailer complaint rests with Volvo Cars Chester.

Despite Volvo UK raising a retailer complaint, repeatedly forwarding my concerns and apologising for Chester's lack of communication, Chester have still never contacted me directly about my complaint.

Their response says they would “do everything we can to help”. Months later, I'm still waiting for them to speak to me.

£10–£15 — cheap/good local independent price

Paid for a timed delivery to a secure garage at the rear of my residence. The parcel was delivered 3 hours early to the side of my house in clear view of the road and pavement. The early delivery and safe location was "authorised" by the sender, which it wasn't. Would recommend to anyone who cannot find any other dodgy delivery companies to accept the job.

EDIT: In regards to company response - The Pallet was 2hrs and 30 minutes early and had been left without authorisation in full view of the path and road. It could have easily been stolen as I was only able to get home for 2pm which was 2 hours after the delivery. You were also not able to come back the same day regardless so it would have had to be left overnight exposed. I had to unload the pallet into my garden and roll a 125kg engine as there was no way for me to lift it and the pallet did not fit through the side gate. I then had to prop up the engine as the pallet had pieces of wood screwed down to stabilise it. The delivery was totally unprofessional and there is no unfairness to my review. 2 hours and a dodgy scrap metal van can easily come along with a couple of stronger works and that engine would have been gone. The correct process would be to deliver the package in the timeslot PAID for, especially when the contact for delivery does not answer the phone as he is working. I had to get friends to come over after work in order to help carry it into the garage. Provide a good service and you get a good review. But for me this is a company to avoid.

one_star_reviews.text: Over promised and under delivered. I recently purchased a set of base units, basin and because I was told that if l cut a template the worktop that would be cut to my specification by the manufacturer. This sale was on a “supply only” basis. I have subsequently noticed that all the 5 star reviews have included the product being fitted by Saffron Bathrooms.  The worktop was unavailable when the base units were delivered and I was in the process of shopping around for an alternative. I then had a call from Morgan saying he was now ready deliver the worktop. I reiterated my concerns about cutting the worktop. He reassured me that one of his fitters lives near me and he would arrange for him to call the following week. This came and went (l had altered long term plans for the fitting). I then started chasing Morgan, the first excuse was that his fitter had stopped answering the phone to him.  As a retired sub contractor, the last person you stop answering the phone to is your employer.  I then made another couple of calls, just to hear the excuses. 2 Fridays’ ago he promised me that he would call me back on the following Monday. Still waiting.  Arranged with a firm l have used previously to cut the top, it wasn’t a problem. If you do want to fit your own suite, just be aware that Morgan over promised and under delivered to me.

one_star_reviews.text:
Extremely Disappointed

A few years ago, my friends and I ordered burgers from this place, and the food was great. Everyone was really happy with it. I’ve been talking to my partner about this place ever since, but we could never really justify the cost when there are so many other places with lower prices and delivery charges.

Today, we saw they had an offer for £8 off £30+ on their set bundles, so we finally decided to give them a try.

We ordered a Smokey Joe’s Burger, a Pepperoni Deluxe Pizza, and Cheesy Chips with Pulled BBQ Beef.

First, we waited over 35 minutes for a collection order. We arrived 10 minutes early, only to be told that they didn’t have the beef and would substitute it with bacon. There was no apology, no compensation, and no attempt to contact us beforehand about the change. We were simply told when we arrived.

The “bacon” they used was some kind of cheap salami that they apparently call bacon. It didn’t taste good and looked even worse. The fries were soggy and completely bland. I’ve genuinely had better fries from vans found in the wild.

The pizza, for something called a “Deluxe Pepperoni Pizza”, was small, disappointing and missing a huge amount of the pepperoni. The pepperoni itself tasted sour, and the dough was honestly the worst I’ve ever tried. It didn’t taste or feel like something that had been properly made or cooked in an authentic way. If I had been given that dough with my eyes closed, I genuinely wouldn’t have been able to tell what kind of burnt bread I was eating.

If we hadn’t been taught never to waste food, we would have definitely thrown most of it in the bin.

The burger was the only thing that actually looked edible, but even that didn’t really taste good. As I said before, I’ve had better burgers from a van in the wild. It was nothing like what I remember having from this same place a few years ago.

I’m extremely disappointed.

It honestly feels like the place may have been sold to new owners and that the kitchen staff have completely changed, because whatever made the food good a few years ago is clearly no longer there.

My kid was so disappointed when he tried the fries, and I couldn’t even give him anything else to try because, after tasting everything ourselves, I was genuinely afraid to give him the food.

I would rather stay hungry than order from this place again. Absolutely nothing about this experience made the price worth it, even with the discount.
